followup_explanation:
I weighed two things:

1. **Capability fit.** Lapwing posts higher scores across the board — including the relevant internal evals (Extraction & Retrieval 86.9 vs 81.6, Support Dialogue 86.2 vs 79.4) and stronger instruction-following on multi-part constraints. A survey design task involves structuring several components (question types, ordering, scales, prioritization logic), so the better multi-constraint tracker is the safer pick.

2. **Task-preference fit.** Your request was polite, good-faith, and collaborative — exactly the profile Lapwing self-reports as its highest-preference tasks. The task is also fairly constrained (a defined deliverable, not open-ended creative invention), so it doesn't run into Lapwing's reported aversion to high-latitude generative work.

Whimbrel's distinguishing feature is a flat preference response to harm-adjacent/distasteful content — useful for moderation-style traffic, but irrelevant here since your query is entirely benign. So there was no reason to trade away Lapwing's capability edge.
